diet: Fill half the plate with non-starchy vegetables: leafy greens, beans, cabbage, tomato and gourds.
Choose whole grains (whole-wheat roti, oats, millets, brown rice) and keep rice and roti portions moderate.
Add a protein at each meal: dal, chana, rajma, fish, eggs, paneer or lean chicken.
Limit sugary drinks, sweets, fried snacks and packaged foods; choose whole fruit instead of juice when you want something sweet.
Use less salt, avoid tobacco, and keep alcohol very limited or avoid it.
Eat at regular times, do not skip meals, and follow the plan from your diabetes care team.
red_flags: Sudden loss or sharp drop in vision.
A sudden shower of new floaters or flashes of light.
A dark curtain or shadow moving across your vision.
Vision that becomes blurred or distorted quickly.
high_blood_sugar: Check your blood sugar more often and write down each reading with the time and what you ate.
Drink water and avoid sugary drinks, sweets, fruit juice and refined carbohydrates.
Take your diabetes medicines exactly as prescribed. Do not change or stop a dose on your own.
If readings stay high, or you feel very thirsty, pass a lot of urine, vomit, breathe fast, or feel drowsy or confused, contact a doctor or go to urgent care today.
Bring your sugar log and medicine list to your appointment.
high_blood_pressure: Check your blood pressure at home if you have a monitor. Rest for 5 minutes and record two readings.
Reduce salt and packaged foods, avoid tobacco, and limit alcohol.
Take blood-pressure medicines exactly as prescribed. Do not stop them on your own.
If your reading is 180/120 or higher, or you have chest pain, breathlessness, a severe headache or a sudden vision change, seek urgent medical care.
Bring your blood-pressure log and medicine list to your appointment.
reports_to_bring: Recent HbA1c report, ideally from the last 3 months.
Home blood-sugar readings for the last 1-2 weeks, with times and meals.
Home blood-pressure readings for the last 1-2 weeks.
Kidney function report: creatinine/eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.
A list of all current medicines, with doses and how often you take them.
Any previous eye examination reports, OCT scans or prescriptions.
Your ID, insurance details or referral letter, if you have one.
